entities.name: 万宝龙 Montblanc 学生龙22 (Vintage)

principles: Separate early and later Montblanc 144 generations instead of merging their specifications.
Treat Student 22 / 学生龙 as an unofficial search alias unless a primary catalogue proves otherwise.
Use dealer measurements only as specimen-level observations.
Leave weight, ink capacity and universal dimensions unknown when no model-scoped primary evidence is available.
Do not copy source images without a verified reusable licence.
method.media_result: No reusable primary media was added: the useful historical photographs found were copyrighted collector or dealer images, and no sufficiently identified open-licence image for either exact model was verified.

sources.title: Meisterstück 100 Years
supports: Montblanc introduced models 142, 144 and 146 in 1949.
The 1960 Linie 60 changed to injection-moulded resin and a slimmer design language.
The official history distinguishes 1950s ebonite/celluloid from modern precious resin.
limitations: The page does not publish a complete model-specific specification or exact production chronology for No. 22.
Its general 1949 narrative contains wording about 149 elsewhere on the page that is not used for the 144 claim.

sources.title: Writing Instruments Service Guide 2024
supports: Use lukewarm water without chemical products for routine fountain-pen cleaning.
Do not fill the cap with water; use a damp lint-free cloth.
limitations: This is current generic care guidance, not an original period manual for either vintage model.
Vintage celluloid, brittle plastic and seized mechanisms may require more conservative specialist handling.

sources.title: No. 144
supports: An early-1950s 144 is documented in green-striped celluloid.
Black, grey-striped and green-striped 144 variants appear in collector and catalogue evidence.
Masterpiece and Made in Germany markings can indicate a non-German export example.
A KEF nib is documented on one specimen.
limitations: The page centres on one collector specimen and should not be used for universal dimensions or nib fitment.
Its bibliography cites a specialist book, but that book was not independently inspected in this retrieval.

sources.title: In which periods were the Montblanc Meisterstück 144 and 146 produced after 1961, and are the models technically comparable?
supports: The Goertz slim-line redesign ended production of the earlier 142, 144 and 146 while 149 continued.
Classic cigar-shaped designs gradually returned from 1979.
The later 144 was marketed as Classique and was subsequently discontinued.
limitations: The page explicitly describes its knowledge base as collector discussion accumulated over more than 20 years.
It does not provide one exact relaunch or discontinuation date for 144.

sources.title: Montblanc Meisterstück 144 — Classique-Vorgänger Füllhalter (eingestellt ca. 2005)
supports: The later 144 is described as a discontinued small Meisterstück using cartridges or a piston converter.
The standard guide lists a 14K gold nib and EF, F, M, OM, B, OB, BB and OBB widths.
The page dates discontinuation to approximately 2005.
limitations: The origin page presented an automated-access gate during this retrieval; its indexed text was cross-checked against the accessible fountainpen.de FAQ and an independent NOS specimen.
Special metal versions and market-specific specimens may not share the standard nib material.

sources.title: Mont Blanc Meisterstück 144 Fountain Pen 1990s Model
supports: A documented 1990s new-old-stock 144 uses its original converter and a single-colour 14K fine nib.
That specimen measures 135.7 mm capped, 12 mm maximum cap diameter and 10 mm maximum section diameter.
The specimen is categorised as cartridge-converter filled.
limitations: Measurements and nib configuration apply to this specimen only, not every 144 generation or finish.
The page is a dealer listing rather than a factory catalogue.

sources.title: Montblanc Meisterstück 144 Gen.2
supports: The specialist chronology separates the early celluloid piston/screw-cap generation from later 144 generations.
It describes the approximately 1995–2004 generation as 14K two-tone, cartridge-converter filled and friction capped.
It identifies 145 as the 2004 replacement with a screw cap and without the corrosion-prone ring ahead of the nib.
limitations: The origin page returned an access error to the browser during this retrieval; claims were available through the search index only.
Its detailed generation dates are a restorer's chronology and are therefore presented as approximate, not official production cut-offs.

sources.title: Montblanc Meisterstück 144 Classique Füllfederhalter
supports: A 1994 144 Classique specimen uses resin, a 14K nib and a cartridge/converter system.
The review lists EF, F, M, B, BB, OM, OB and OBB nib choices and compares 144 with 145.
It describes 144 as discontinued and 145 as the then-current alternative.
limitations: Measurements and writing impressions belong to the author's specimen.
The article was published in 2015, so its statement about current availability is used only with a live Montblanc Classique product page.

sources.title: Meisterstück Classique Fountain Pen
supports: Montblanc currently markets a Meisterstück Classique under Ident No. MB132581VG.
The current product page describes black precious resin, three platinum-coated rings and an Au585/14K nib.
limitations: The public product page does not use the historical 145 number in its product title.
Current specifications are intentionally not copied into the vintage 144 model fields.

sources.title: Montblanc Classic pens (1960–2010)
supports: No. 22 belongs to the Medium range and demi-size class, not the Economy range.
The 22/24 configuration is documented as push cap, wide-plus-thin cap bands, 14K wing nib, piston filler and wide blue ink window.
A transcription of the 1969 North American catalogue describes No. 22 with 14K nib, 1/20 14K gold-filled trim and a 25-year guarantee.
The same catalogue transcription lists flexible EF/F/M/B/BB and rigid EF nib choices for No. 22.
Parts interchange across 12/22/32-family pens creates a material risk of cap, nib-unit or body chimeras.
limitations: This is an independent synthesis combining catalogues, collector sites and the author's specimens, not a Montblanc publication.
The linked catalogue image was not treated as a separately verified archive locator in this source record.
The author's general writing-feel observations are not used as universal claims.

sources.title: Montblanc 22
supports: The page catalogues Montblanc 22 as a 1960–1970 model.
Its specimen photographs provide an independent visual cross-check for the model and nib form.
limitations: The page provides a date range and images but little textual specification.
The photographs are copyrighted and were not reused.

sources.title: Montblanc 22 Fountain Pen (1960s) — Black, Piston Fill, 14k Broad Nib
supports: One 1960s specimen has Model 22 engraved on the cap band, a tested piston filler, blue-tinted ink window and 14K broad nib.
That specimen measures 5-1/8 inches capped.
Its broad nib was springy but explicitly not described as flexible.
limitations: Length, nib width and writing feel describe one dealer specimen only.
The page is a sales record, not an official catalogue.

sources.title: Montblanc — Vintage Pens 1960ies to present
supports: Multiple 1961 No. 22 specimens are catalogued with piston filling and 14K nibs in F, M or B.
One No. 22 specimen is recorded at approximately 130 mm long and 12.9 mm cap diameter.
limitations: The page is a long specialist sales/specimen database and individual records may reflect owner attribution.
Dimensions and nib behaviour remain specimen-level evidence.

unresolved.reason: No model-scoped primary source covering all 144 generations was verified; specialist chronologies differ slightly.
No direct Montblanc catalogue scan with a stable verified locator was obtained for these claims; existing evidence either contradicts the nickname or is specimen/community-level.
